texts.orig: This manuscript is structured as follows. we introduce the main concepts of controlled rough paths and control functions required in this setting: We specify that we consider (p; ~)-rough X for p and define suitable controlled rough paths according to X Our definition is a natural generalization of the controlled rough paths according to a monotone scale of interpolation spaces introduced in GHN21] . Here we incorporate in Definition 2.6 more iterated integrals and decrease the spatial regularity of the Gubinelli derivatives and remainders according to the time regularity of the rough path X. The main innovative aspect in comparison to GHN21 is the replacement of the corresponding Hõlder norms of the rough input X and of the controlled rough path with suitable control functions. These are necessary in order to establish the desired integrable bounds and represent a main technical ingredient of our work. To our best knowledge; this is the first suitable Banach spaces in terms of control functions instead of Hõlder continuity. Afterwards we construct a rough integral for such controlled rough paths against X. This is naturally achieved by Sewing lemma stated in Theorem 2.11, keeping track of several parameters reflecting an interplay between the time regularity of X; the loss of spatial regularity ~, the number of iterated integrals and the parameter p arising in the definition of the (p; ~)-rough path chosen such that ơ p < ~ and of the control function. As already mentioned, the main technical challenge is to incorporate the control functions in our arguments. paths

texts.orig: Section 3 establishes the well-posedness of (1.1) based on the properties of the rough integral introduced in Section 2. This can be achieved by a standard fixed-point argument in the space of controlled rough introduced in Section 2 We provide the necessary steps required in order to set up this argument relying on the assumption that the diffusion coefficient G is linear. As already mentioned, one could incorporate a nonlinear term G which is N + 1 Fréchet differentiable with bounded derivatives. In this case; our techniques combined with a standard fixed-point argument as in [GH19, GHN21] entail the local well-posedness of (1.1). An additional boundedness assumption on the Fréchet derivatives up to order N + 1 as in [HN22] will imply the global-intime existence Such boundedness assumptions have been relaxed for rough differential equations in [LY25]. We refrain from providing the details of the fixed-point argument and focus instead on establishing moment bounds for (1.1). paths
